title: Oat flour for all the flour in a dough that rises

evidence.basis: D-5: DISPUTED, so not offered; not a finding that it can't work. OD-7 (owner commission 2026-10-08, ENGINEERING only; not culinary validation, not released guidance). Evidence: private/research/substitution-knowledge (2026-10-07). KA SRC-FS-13#a (up to half, non-yeasted); Bob's Red Mill SRC-FS-39#a (up to 20%); Quaker SRC-FS-45#c (all of it, if the bake doesn't need to rise) and #d (about 1/3 when relying on gluten for rise). The research candidate oat_flour_for_all_flour_in_chemically_leavened_dough and the retained AI card ('Oat flour for the plain flour', v2 shortcake) are kept as records.

text: CourseCorrect doesn't offer oat flour in place of all the flour in this dough: for a dough that has to rise, the sources disagree (King Arthur Baking says up to half, Bob's Red Mill up to a fifth; Quaker allows all of it only when the bake doesn't need to rise).
scopeNote: This is about replacing all of the flour here. It isn't a verdict on oat-flour recipes or on using some oat flour.
answer: isn't offered here, because the sources disagree
